consumerSurface.derivation: Parse the pinned Python source with ast; enumerate every Call whose receiver is d9mod or authorities['d9mod']; retain its full chained attribute path, source line, positional arity and keyword names.
consumerSurface.closureRule: Every AST-derived call path must resolve at runtime; each callable is invoked with its frozen-consumer arity. A predecessor-diff or declared-list-presence check is not a consumer-surface proof.

authenticatedRestoration.loadRule: V17 is the real module handle produced by executing pinned check-d9-v1.7.py bytes inside the authenticated v1.8 chain; its V16 is likewise produced from pinned check-d9.py bytes. No unverified filesystem-path import may supply either module.
authenticatedRestoration.publicCheckAdapter: check(candidate, predecessor, v16) first requires predecessor and v16 to equal the pinned v1.7/v1.6 data snapshots, then calls the authenticated v1.8 checker. v1.11 artifact validation remains private to the CLI and is not an overload of this public API.

No class, code, exit, axis, union, map, reducer, precedence, golden, identity, generic scope, remedy, or v1.10 reviewed semantic changes are permitted.

This is a checker-API compatibility probe, not a complete RT15 rebind and not acceptance or application of the rejected v1.8 authority.

codeVocabulary.rule: A code outside this vocabulary is a contract violation. Codes are grouped by remedy: two codes with the same remedy are a smell, two remedies behind one code is a defect.

spellingMigration.note: The canonical spelling choice is arbitrary; the CLOSURE requirement is not. v1.3 declared a closed vocabulary and shipped 12 error codes plus 5 reason codes outside it — the retained checker (D5) is what makes that impossible to repeat.

deficiency.why: Which Coverage/verdict deficiency applies. Without it, coverage-missing and provider-unavailable share axes yet carry different remedies.

rejectionCause.why: Which request rejection applies. identity-expired requires tombstone evidence; identity-unknown is its absence — the distinction A2-D9-V12-05 required and the v1.4 enum rewrite regressed.

faultCause.why: Which operational fault applies. Distinguishes contention (retry) from corruption (repair).

secondaryDeficiencies.why: A Run can genuinely carry more than one deficiency (no TS provider AND an exhausted Rust budget). v1.5 had one deficiency slot, so the extra reason codes on the wire were unconstrained: B-D9V15-03 showed a second reasonCode could be appended and the checker exited 0. The ordered code list is now derived in full from (deficiency, secondaryDeficiencies), so an undeclared code is rejected.

invariants.text: Only the host finalizer constructs HostTermination; one map class→exitCode; one controllable process-exit write site.
For finite CLI commands, CommandEnvelope.termination equals process termination when serialization succeeds.
FailureResult is constructible without project or Run identity.
Policy verdict never becomes Error; operational failure never becomes Finding.
Optional Cloud/export failure cannot alter local Run verdict.
Durability failure cannot report success for an authoritative Run.

RunId is externally observable only for a committed Run. A failed final authoritative commit omits runId, retains executionId for attempt correlation, and cannot expose a pre-commit candidate identity.

Any HOST-DERIVED admitted Run finalization precondition whose frozen authoritative target is proven unsatisfiable terminates request-rejected/REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE with its ExecutionId and no Run identity. D9 maps that normalized state and its fresh-Attempt remedy; it does not authenticate source or provenance.
There is a finalization commit point after HostTermination is settled and required postconditions evaluated. Signals before it may yield interrupted; signals after it cannot reclassify termination.
Interruption/crash during authoritative publication leaves ledger recoverable; orphans are abandoned, never sealed success.
Envelope projects verdict and HostTermination as distinct fields.
Exit 0 alone is never a durable attestation; authority is a required postcondition.
IDENTITY.EXPIRED requires a retained RunId tombstone; otherwise IDENTITY.UNKNOWN.
Unsupported/unnegotiable fingerprint recipe: comparisonPerformed=false and comparisonDerivedFindingCount=0.

rules: A valid empty query result is success; absence is data unless the command addresses one required identity or uses a single-identity resolver.

A query with an explicit completeness requirement that cannot be met is indeterminate.
Baseline compare against an unsupported/unnegotiable fingerprint recipe is indeterminate (never policy-failed via mass false net-new).

Host, datastore, provider-protocol, installation-I/O, ledger busy-timeout, required-delivery, and output-serialization failures are operational-failed; errorCodes distinguish retryable contention from corruption.
A mutation with a linked verification Run propagates that Run's success, policy-failed, indeterminate, or operational-failed termination while retaining the mutation receipt.

A protocol server that shuts down normally OR completes cooperative SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup is success; a host/protocol fault is operational-failed; user-interrupt class is not used for clean serve stop.

peerReviewRequired: Blind re-authoring of the axes for a sample of the 45 goldens by an agent who did not write them — the v1.3 co-consistency trap is structural and only a second author closes it.
Is the faultCause > rejectionCause > deficiency precedence right? It is argued from trust degradation, not measured.
Is secondaryDeficiencies the correct single exception to cause exclusivity, or does rejectionCause need the same treatment?

A different agent who authored neither v1.12 nor its checker must verify stable input hashes, exact ordered-object projections, canonical full-file bytes, every protected raw span and lexical leaf, the complete AST-derived frozen RT14 runtime surface, authenticated source snapshots, predecessor suites and the disposable RT14 API probe. The v1.12 author also authored the v1.11 rejection review and cannot approve this successor.
knownLimitations: The derivation and the goldens still share one author. --selftest proves the checker rejects specific mutations; it cannot prove the axes describe the scenarios truthfully. Only a blind second author closes that, and B-D9V15-05 found exactly this class of defect in v1.5.
The precedence order is a judgment about which remedy a caller should act on first. It is defensible but unmeasured.
$RUN_ID / $COVERAGE_ID / $EXECUTION_ID are placeholders; the goldens prove shape and code derivation, not identifier production.
45 goldens exercise every cause enum value at least once, but not every combination of the remaining nine axes. Full cross-product is 10^5-ish and would not be more convincing.
finalizationTransitions still asserts settled terminations are unchanged by construction — the table is a statement of the rule, not evidence an implementation obeys it.

v1.11 remains rejected and is retained only as runtime/semantic lineage plus repair input. v1.12 is author-produced, not independently reviewed or applied; no RT15 exists, and E8, RT14 and OP6 remain unrejoined. Checker greenness is checker-scope evidence only and grants no product, integration, application or seal authority.

codeMaps.rule: These maps are total and injective. The derivation returns (class, code); a golden whose code disagrees with its axes fails D6.

causeModel.exclusivity: At most ONE cause family is non-none on a termination payload. All 43 goldens already satisfied this in v1.5, but it was never stated or checked, so two authors could encode the same scenario with contradictory causes and both pass (B-D9V15-03).
causeModel.precedenceRule: Concurrent conditions are real. The host REDUCES a concurrent condition set to one terminating cause using this order, then emits that cause alone. Trust degrades in this order: if the host malfunctioned, its rejection and coverage assessments are both untrustworthy; if the request was invalid, its coverage assessment never happened.
causeModel.whyNotMultiCauseOnTheWire: TO-7: a code is a REMEDY CLASS. A caller reading a termination is deciding what to do next and can only act on one thing first. Concurrent secondary conditions are recorded in the Run's Coverage and diagnostics, which is where a human looks; they are not on the termination.
causeModel.theOneException: secondaryDeficiencies. Multiple deficiencies share ONE remedy shape (widen the evidence) and a caller that hits two genuinely needs both, so the deficiency family alone carries an ordered list. It does not cross families: a deficiency never accompanies a fault or a rejection.
causeModel.codeDerivation: The FULL ordered code list is derived, not authored. indeterminate: reasonCodes = [map(deficiency)] + [map(d) for d in secondaryDeficiencies]. request-rejected / operational-failed: errorCode = map(cause). success / policy-failed / interrupted: no code field may be present.

crossAxisInvariants.rule: at most one of (deficiency, rejectionCause, faultCause) is non-none

crossAxisInvariants.why: A2-D9-V12-05: expiry is only distinguishable from never-existed when the address was actually resolved.
A rejected request never entered execution, so no other lifecycle value is truthful.

crossAxisInvariants.rule: class == success -> verdict in (pass, advisory, not-applicable)
crossAxisInvariants.why: TO-5: no path to exit 0 through a failing or indeterminate verdict.
invariant-durability: a durability failure can never report success.

A1-D9-V15-03 asked for interruption=none on serve graceful stop. REJECTED: a graceful stop IS a signal before finalization and recording otherwise would make the axis false — the same defect as B-D9V15-05, which A1 raised itself. The real risk A1 identified is that class flips if derive's clause order changes; this invariant closes that order-independently, which the proposed fix would not.

crossAxisInvariants.rule: secondaryDeficiencies non-empty -> deficiency != none, no duplicates, primary not repeated

commandKind == run AND admission == admitted AND lifecycle == cannot-seal-coherent-run AND domainCondition == precondition-failed AND rejectionCause == unsatisfiable -> class == request-rejected, durability == not-applicable, requiredPostconditions == not-applicable, deficiency == none, faultCause == none
crossAxisInvariants.why: Every HOST-DERIVED admitted finalization precondition already classified unsatisfiable has the same fresh-Attempt remedy. D9 consumes that normalized classification without authenticating provenance; the owning domain contract must prove the frozen authoritative target cannot complete.

adjudicationRevision.note: Adjudication: concurrent-condition reducer becomes executable; scenario prose made self-sufficient; any-kind lifecycle redefined as host-finalization projection; checker reads causeModel, crossAxisInvariants, commandKind sync.

inputSchema.description: Pre-reduction concurrent conditions observed by the host before wire emission

algorithm: If any faultCauses non-empty: terminating family=faultCause; pick first faultCauses[0]; drop rejection and deficiency from wire.
Else if any rejectionCauses non-empty: terminating family=rejectionCause; pick first; drop deficiency from wire.

Else if any deficiencies non-empty: terminating family=deficiency; primary=deficiencies[0]; secondaryDeficiencies = remaining deficiencies + declared secondaryDeficiencies (deduped, primary excluded).
concurrentConditionReducer.output: exclusive scenarioAxes cause triple with at most one family non-none

hostDerivedUnsatisfiableFinalizationCont.scope: Every HOST-DERIVED normalized admitted Run finalization precondition satisfying the exact derivation predicate below. Every matching tuple receives the same REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE and fresh-Attempt remedy.
hostDerivedUnsatisfiableFinalizationCont.upstreamProducerObligation: Before emitting rejectionCause=unsatisfiable on this admitted finalization path, the owning domain contract must mechanically prove that the Run's frozen authoritative target cannot be completed. D9 does not authenticate that source or provenance.

consumerProfile.description: Authorized retention expiry is one concrete example, not a D9 source discriminator.

derivationBranch.scopeHonesty: Every normalized tuple satisfying this exact predicate maps identically. D9 has no source or provenance axis and deliberately neither authenticates nor discriminates provenance.

remedyEquivalence.beforeAdmission: restore or restate the unavailable required authority before asking for an authoritative Run
remedyEquivalence.afterAdmission: restore or restate the unavailable required authority and submit a fresh Attempt
remedyEquivalence.sameAutomationDisposition: The current request cannot be completed under its frozen authoritative target; changing or restoring prerequisites and resubmitting is required.

identityContract.retry: The settled ExecutionId is terminal. Any later attempt after authority restoration receives a new ExecutionId; semantic identities remain independent of either ExecutionId.
identityContract.computedResult: Coverage and verdict already returned by CoreCompletion remain visible only as NON-AUTHORITATIVE-ATTEMPT-DIAGNOSTIC values. They are not a Run verdict and cannot mint a Run identity.

faultPrecedenceControl.rule: The existing faultCause > rejectionCause > deficiency reducer is byte-identical and remains authoritative.
